items.title: Continuous coefficients along a compact-state progressive process

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib compact-state coefficient lemma, statement seal; Mathlib MemLp.of_bound provides the product-space bound.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplementary lemma. The linked Mathlib declaration provides background on bounded-function integrability.

items.statement: Let X be a jointly measurable, strongly progressive process taking values in a compact second-countable pseudometrizable Borel state space S. Let c be a continuous real function of nonnegative time and state. Then the coefficient evaluated along X is strongly progressive. For each finite nonnegative horizon its time section is integrable at every sample. With a finite sample measure, the sample-first product representative belongs to $L^p$ for every exponent p in the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: The sample space carries a finite measure and a filtration indexed by nonnegative time. The horizon T is nonnegative and finite. The integrability exponent p is any extended nonnegative real, including zero and infinity.
The state space S is compact, second countable and pseudometrizable, with its Borel sigma-algebra. The process is jointly measurable and strongly progressive.
The real coefficient c is jointly continuous on nonnegative time times S. The horizon time measure is Lebesgue time restricted to [0,T] on the nonnegative real axis.

obligations.label: Compose the progressive process with a continuous coefficient and prove horizon integrability.

bindings.boundary: The claim is coefficient regularity and finite-horizon integrability for a given process. Progressive measurability is global; the time-section and product bounds are local to the chosen horizon.

assumption_deltas.source: Jointly measurable and strongly progressive compact-state process with a continuous scalar coefficient.
assumption_deltas.lean: Both measurability interfaces are explicit; the state type has the second-countable pseudometrizable Borel structure used by product measurability.
assumption_deltas.reason: The product measurable map supplies time sections, while the filtration-window interface supplies strong progressiveness.

assumption_deltas.source: Every sample time section is integrable over each finite horizon and the product representative is in every L^p for finite sample measure.
assumption_deltas.lean: Section integrability is universally quantified over samples; p ranges over ENNReal. The product measure has sample first and nonnegative time second.
assumption_deltas.reason: One uniform bound over the compact horizon and state space gives both conclusions with the indicated measure orientation.
